subject: Career
title: Recommendation Networks: Who Vouches for You
description: A fast breakdown of Recommendation Networks: Who Vouches for You for builders.

hook.text: A hiring manager emails your former colleague: 'What's she really like to work with?' Your brand depends on the answer.

buildup.text: Formal references are staged. Informal back-channel references are where truth flows.

discovery.text: Your recommendation network is the set of people who will vouch for you unsolicited.

twist.text: You build this network not by asking for favors but by being consistently excellent and kind.

climax.text: Every interaction is a deposit or withdrawal from your recommendation bank.

punchline.text: Your brand isn't what you say. It's what they say.

quiz.question: What builds a strong recommendation network?
options: Being consistently excellent and kind in every interaction

details.summary: A recommendation network is the group of people who would actively vouch for you in professional settings. The strength, diversity, and seniority of your recommendation network directly influences your career opportunities and job search success.
details.whyItMatters: References and informal endorsements remain among the most powerful hiring influencers. A strong recommendation network means doors open proactively, not just when you push them.
takeaways: Cultivate recommenders across different organizations and seniority levels
Keep potential recommenders updated on your career trajectory
Reciprocate by being a strong recommender for others

faq.question: How many active recommenders should you maintain in your network?
faq.answer: Aim for six to ten people across different relationships: former managers, peers, direct reports, and clients. This diversity provides coverage for different types of opportunities and ensures you always have appropriate references available.

faq.question: How do you maintain relationships with recommenders between active job searches?
faq.answer: Send periodic updates about your career progress, congratulate them on their achievements, and offer help when you can. A brief touchpoint every three to six months keeps the relationship warm so that a reference request never feels like it comes from nowhere.
